title: Approvals: refuse an approval that cannot show itself on a closing field when it opens, and never write a closed value for an abandoned request (ADR-0162 item 7)
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ③ maintainer-directed · Source: ADR-0162 Execution item 7 (accepted by merge 972114df)

## 维护者速读

- 做什么：对象在审批状态字段上声明了「已关闭」时，平台在发起审批那一刻检查配置；配置会让单据停在一个没走完的审批结果上的，直接拒绝发起并说明缺什么。审批被撤回时，平台不再把状态写回已关闭的值。
- 用户会看到什么：配置不合格时，提交人发起审批会失败并看到原因，作者在编写时会先收到提示；撤回一张原本已批准又被重新送审的单据后，单据保持打开，需要重新审批。
- 不做会怎样：多步审批中途撤回或卡住，单据可能显示「已批准」并锁死，而实际上后面的审批没走完。
- 顺序：和「声明与执行」那张卡同一次发布；声明不能在这张卡之前对外可用。

## What happens

The approval status mirror writes a request's status onto the field its step names (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts#mirrorStatusField`). Once an object can close on that field (item 1), three things on `main` would leave a document reading a decision its approval did not finish, and closed:

- A request that is abandoned, by its submitter's recall, by an administrator's override or by the sweep of a dead run, has the value the field held at submit put back. Where that value is a closed one, the document is closed again over edits no approval has seen.
- An approval of several steps can stop between two of them with the earlier step's outcome on the field: a later step that mirrors onto another field or none, a write or a pause between two steps, a `pending` the field cannot show.
- A request does not know which approval it belongs to. A child run knows only its immediate parent, and the two stamps a request carries live in its config snapshot, which the store cannot filter on.

The maintainer ruled both rules on 2026-11-26, on #36253: 「平台堵住：撤回不恢复关闭值」 (ruling record 7201405662, with the chosen option's text on 7202242844) and 「平台拒绝这种配置」 (ruling record 7205949718). ADR-0162 D5 carries them. The conditions below spell the second ruling out further than its option's words do; the record says so and the maintainer's merge adopted it.

## Expected

Four slices, released with item 1.

**A. The root run.**
- The automation service hands every run of a tree, to any depth, its root run: that run's id, the flow it was started on, the object of its record and when it started.
- The approval node passes it to the plugin, and each request records its root run as it opens, in a column of its own that the store can be asked for.
- A run started before this change gets its root run when the service resumes it, derived from the run's links to its parents, so that every request opened after the release records one.
- This slice changes the automation service as well as the plugin, and owes its own semver judgement.

**B. The check when an approval opens (D5, "An approval opens on a closing field only where the field can show it in progress").**
- At an approval's first request the node reads every approval step of the root run's flow and of each flow a `subflow` or a `map` in it names, to any depth, with each step's own mirror field and each object the step can act on, a `map`'s item object included.
- Where the object closes on a step's field at `pending`, `returned`, `approved` or `rejected`, the request is refused unless all of this holds:
  1. the field declares `pending`, and the object closes on neither `pending` nor `returned`;
  2. a `state_machine` rule on the field that declares the moves out of a closed `approved` or `rejected` has `pending` among them;
  3. the field carries no `readonlyWhen`, and none of its options for a request's status carries a `visibleWhen`;
  4. every approval step that can act on a record of the object names that field, a step in a `map` body counting as one that can act on the parent's record;
  5. no flow of the approval that runs as the user holds a node that can write the record or a line of it between two steps;
  6. no flow of the approval holds a node there that can pause the run, and the approval holds no `map` with an approval step in its body, at any depth, unless the node shows that none of its items is a record.
- Between two steps is after one step's closed outcome and before the next step opens. The next step can be the same step opened again, so a node after the last step of a `map` body stands between two steps. The revise window of a returned request is not such a pause.
- A node whose writes the check cannot read counts as one that writes. A node it cannot place counts as standing between two steps. An approval it cannot read whole is refused.
- A later request of the same approval is not judged again. A request the plugin cannot place as first or later is not judged.
- An object that closes on the field only on values of its own is asked nothing. In an application with no declaration nothing is read.
- The refusal names what is missing. The same conditions are reported at authoring wherever the parts are in view together.

**C. The mirror on an abandoned request (D5, "An abandoned approval never writes a closed value").**
- On every transition that abandons a request the mirror reads the object's closed values for the mirror field and never writes one, `recalled` included.
- Where there is no `recalled` value it may write, it goes down the order: the value held at submit, the field's declared default, empty. A closed value is passed over at each step, and on a required field an empty value at submit is passed over for the default.
- A closed value the approval did not write is left alone. The mirror places the abandoned request by its root run and asks its own table, in one probe, whether a request of the same approval on the same record had the value the field holds. Where it cannot tell, it goes down the order.
- Every other write of the mirror is unchanged, and so is every write on an object that closes on no value of the mirror field.

**D. The approvals guide.**
- What an abandoned approval leaves; what a field and a flow owe an approval on an object that closes on its outcome; what a refused opening is for the person who submitted.
- It names the one mirror field for every step and the pause that may not stand between two steps, says that an approval of each item under a `map` runs as an approval of its own, and that an approval which does not mirror onto the closing field does not open a closed document.
- It keeps the word "round" for the resubmissions of ADR-0044.

## Carried from the contract reviews of ADR-0162

These are review notes the reviews sent to this card. Each is answered in the PR.

- **A node type with no descriptor (N43).** "Counts as one that can pause" means a type that has an executor and publishes no descriptor. The two structural types, `start` and `end`, have no executor and cannot pause, so the `end` of a `map` body or of a `subflow` body refuses nothing. A test pins a `map` whose items are written out and whose body ends in `end`. The docs tell the author that a node type without a descriptor between two approval steps is refused.
- **The `map` rule is meant of the parent's object (N44).** A `map` is refused where the parent's object closes on the field of a step that can act on its record. Two arms are pinned as not refused: an item's object that closes on the body step's field under a parent whose object does not; and a parent run that carries no record, the batch sign-off shape the showcase ships.
- **Error or notice at authoring (N45).** The record says the conditions are "reported" at authoring. The option the maintainer chose says 报错, an error. This card states which it is where the object and the flow are in view together, and gives the reason. A refusal at publish as well, where the pair is in view, is the reading nearest the option's words, and ADR-0162's Alternatives does not list it: the card takes it or says why not.
- **An empty put-back on both kinds of field (N17).** The record validator refuses an update that empties a required field only when the field is not `readonly`. It does not make that refusal for a `readonly` field, for a `system` column, or for a field that is required only when shown. The approval node's schema advises a `readonly` mirror field. The tests run the put-back on each configuration and pin the value the field keeps.
- **Tests counted by transition (N20).** The override arm of `recall` admits a system context as well as an administrator. The abandonment tests are counted by the transition that abandons a request, not by who acts.
- **A trace when the mirror withholds a value (N21).** The mirror warns today when it leaves a status unwritten because the field does not declare it. It also logs when it withholds a declared `recalled` or passes over a closed value, so that an author who closed on `recalled` can find why the field reads the default.

## Done when

- [ ] Slice A: a child run that was started before the release and opens a request after it records its root run. The automation-service change carries its own changeset and semver line.
- [ ] Slice B: a test for each missing condition, and for each arm ADR-0162 Execution item 7 lists under "Its tests cover", among them: an object that closes only on values of its own; an application with no declaration; a step that names no mirror field or another field, ahead of and after a step the conditions concern; a `map` with an approval step in its body ahead of the parent's steps, between two of them and after the last, with its items read from an expression and written out in the node; a step two levels down; two child runs side by side; a flow the node cannot read; a writing node between two steps in a flow that runs as the user and in one that runs as system; a `wait` and a `screen` between two steps; the revise window; a `visibleWhen` on each status option; a later request of an approval that opened before the declaration; a later request whose earlier requests record no root run.
- [ ] Slice C: the tests ADR-0162 Execution item 7 lists under "The mirror", across the three writers that abandon a request, among them: a field that declares `recalled` as an open value, as a closed value and not at all; a value at submit that is closed, open, empty on a required field, empty on a field that is not required, and not carried by the request; a field that holds a closed value the approval did not write; an earlier step's outcome with that step in the same run, in a child run and in the parent; a `map` in which only another item's request had the value; a request that records no root run; a default that is usable, closed or absent.
- [ ] The six carried notes above are each answered, with the test or the sentence named.
- [ ] Slice D is in the approvals guide.
- [ ] A refused opening reaches the person who submitted as a failed run whose message says what is missing, in every locale the plugin carries.
- [ ] The release rule holds: the key (item 1) is not published before slices A, B and C are in the same release.

Category ③: maintainer-directed. A build card of ADR-0162, child of #36253.
Grade: area:data · Feature · n/a (not a defect on `main`; it becomes one the day the key ships without it) · reach: every approval on an object that closes on its approval field · evidence: read (ADR-0162 D5 and its Readings; eleven contract reviews of PR #37606)
Suggested-grade: p2 · it gates the release of #36253's key, so it takes the grade of the card it blocks
Size: L (the automation service, the approvals plugin, a new column, the authoring report, the guide). Split along slices A to D before dispatch; A goes first and can land on `main` alone.
Business reason: carried from #36253 and the two rulings quoted above. A document must not read a decision, and be closed on it, when its approval did not finish.
Reader: seat 2 (repo:objectstack#2), one card thread per slice, effort high.
Release-order: slices B and C read the object's closed values, so they need item 1's key on the same trunk branch; they are not blocked on `main`. Slice A is blocked by nothing.
Clause-②: yes (widening) for slice A: a new member on what the automation service hands a node, and a new column on the request. No for B, C and D taken alone.
Metadata-protocol: none while the key is unpublished. The release that publishes the key carries `added`, and the conditions are part of what that key means; the seat confirms the line at the claim.
Dedupe: searched `mirrorStatusField` (open issues): 0 hits. Searched `closedStates` (all issues): 1 hit, #36253 itself.
Related: #36253, PR #37606 (ADR-0162), ADR-0044 (rounds of a request), the card for item 8 (what the check cannot read ahead).

Dispatch note: the card thread also reads the seat's private memo for this card before it starts.
